title: Orange5 AtomSmasher AIR Frame v0
description: Anti-Inflation Recursive (AIR) codec output frame. Represents the dense, structure-extracted form of verbose model output. The AIR codec lifts facts, claims, citations, decisions, numbers, dates, identifiers, and code spans out of free prose and drops filler (hedges, throat-clearing, transitional fluff, ceremonial closers). The frame is the canonical wire shape: an integrity-tagged container that round-trips losslessly for the structured slots and lossily-by-design for the prose slot. Decompression reconstructs a readable (not byte-identical) rendition from the structured slots, so receipts MUST hash the FRAME, never the reconstructed prose.

frame_id.description: SHA-256 hex digest over canonical-JSON of all extracted slots (facts, claims, citations, numbers, dates, identifiers, code_spans, decisions, questions, residue). frame_id is independent of created_at and source_hash so two callers compressing semantically identical input arrive at the same frame_id.

source_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the verbatim input string the codec compressed. Lets a receipt-holder prove what was fed in without storing the input.

original_chars.description: Character length of the input string (UTF-16 code units, JavaScript .length convention). Integrity slot; the compression_ratio is computed from this.

compressed_chars.description: Character length of the canonical-JSON serialization of the structured slots (everything inside the frame EXCEPT schema, frame_id, source_hash, original_chars, compressed_chars, compression_ratio, created_at). The codec optimises to make this number small.

compression_ratio.description: compressed_chars / max(original_chars, 1). Below 1.0 means we compressed. Above 1.0 means the structure cost more than the prose saved (rare; surfaces as a warning, not a failure).

facts.description: Atomic factual statements lifted from the source. Each fact is a single declarative kernel — subject + verb + object — stripped of qualifiers and connective tissue. Ordered by first appearance.

claims.description: Assertions the source makes that are NOT independently verifiable from the source text alone. Claims differ from facts in that they carry an implicit 'according to <speaker>' wrapper. Each entry includes the claim text and a confidence cue if the source provided one (otherwise null).

confidence.description: Hedge / certainty signal lifted from the surrounding prose, normalized: 'asserted' | 'hedged' | 'speculative' | null.

citations.description: Citations lifted from the source: URLs, DOIs, arXiv ids, RFC numbers, repo paths, statute citations, file paths. Each entry is the citation token plus a short context window from the source (the half-sentence that referenced it).

numbers.description: Numeric values with their units and the half-sentence context. Captures the 'load-bearing numbers' a verbose answer would bury in prose.

dates.description: Calendar dates / ISO timestamps / relative time anchors found in the source. Raw form preserved; normalized ISO 8601 added when parseable.

identifiers.description: Named entities, proper nouns, code identifiers, brand names, and operator-personal references that should round-trip exactly. The codec preserves these verbatim; lossy reconstruction MUST NOT paraphrase them.

code_spans.description: Code / command / config snippets lifted out of the prose. Preserved byte-exact so the receipt holder can rerun them. Each entry retains the source language hint when present.

decisions.description: Imperative / declarative commitments the source makes: 'will do X', 'shipping by Y', 'ruling out Z'. Decisions are kernels that downstream modules (Commitment Atoms, Equation Store) may promote to atoms.

questions.description: Open questions the source raises but does not answer. Used by routing layers to spawn follow-ups.

residue.description: The minimum prose fragments that could not be cleanly slotted into facts/claims/citations/etc. but carry enough signal that dropping them would lose information. Kept short and ordered by source position. If the codec did its job, residue is small.

dropped.description: Audit slot. Each entry is a short tag plus the count of characters dropped under that tag. Lets a reviewer prove what was thrown away. Tags include: 'hedge', 'fluff', 'transition', 'pleasantry', 'self_reference', 'whitespace'.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the frame was minted at. Not included in frame_id (so identical input -> identical frame_id regardless of when compressed).

notes.description: Optional reviewer notes. The codec itself never writes here; reserved for downstream annotators.
